title: Tulane University-Ochsner Health Genomic Precision Medicine Program
text:
The Tulane University / Ochsner Health Genomic Precision Medicine Program and its Health Education
through Robust Omics and Individualized Care (HEROIC) mission will develop the next generation of
biomedical researchers equipped with the latest tools to gather and analyze data to understand challenges and
to deploy interventions to improve health disparities in our region. Our proposed predoctoral T32 training
program includes a dynamic partnership between Tulane University and Ochsner Health in New
Orleans, Louisiana that would be the first NHGRI-funded training program located in an Institutional
Development Awards (IDeA) state. Working with mentors from Tulane University and co-mentors from
Ochsner Health, our trainees will identify a health condition in the local New Orleans region that is relevant
nationally, and design a genomic precision medicine project.

title: Translational Imaging and Behavioral Assessment (TIBA)
text: Translational Imaging & Behavioral Assessment (TIBA) Core Cognitive Neuroscience of Development and Aging (CoNDA) Center Critical to understanding the basis of neurocognition and behavior is the imaging of brain structure and function, and ultimately linking these measures to behavioral and cognitive phenotypes. The Translational Imaging and Behavioral Assessment (TIBA) Core of the Cognitive Neuroscience of Development and Aging (CoNDA) Center in Phase II will support Research Project Leaders (RPLs) and Pilot Project Investigators (PPLs) who are performing research in animal models of neurocognitive disorders. The TIBA Core will also be available to other investigators across the CoNDA Campus. The TIBA Core will provide shared centralized research resources that provide access to technologies, instruments, as well as expert consultation and other services to scientific preclinical investigators. The core is composed of three sub-cores to support imaging and behavioral experiments. The Small Animal Magnetic Resonance Imaging (SAMRI) sub-core provides structural and functional imaging on a broader scale. The Intravital Imaging sub-core provides access to a multiphoton microscope and a fluorescent light sheet microscope for functional and structural, cellular and circuit analysis of animal brains. Finally, the Animal Behavior sub-core provides a broad panel of behavioral and cognitive assessments in translational models for neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders. The TIBA Core was established during the second year of Phase I and has grown tremendously in types of services provided and number of users and grants it supported. The TIBA Core will be directed by Dr. Dunaevsky (overall TIBA), with sub-cores directed by Dr. Liu (SAMRI), Dr. Jensen-Smith (Intravital Imaging), and Dr. Samuelson (Animal Behavior).

title: Cancer Neuroscience Training Program
text:
An emerging new discipline termed “Cancer Neuroscience” addresses functional interactions between tumors
and the nervous system. We propose a training program that will enable doctorate level basic scientists to
work within this new field. Our trainees will address therapeutic challenges and develop new medicines for
cancers and for a variety of neurologic disease states.

title: Development of an Oral Microbiome Foundation Model for Systemic Diseases Assessment
text:
This project will develop a novel Oral Microbiome Foundation Model (OMFM) leveraging extensive oral
microbiome samples and advanced deep learning (Transformer-based architecture). By addressing limitations
of disease-specific datasets and conventional analysis methods, OMFM will establish a scalable, population-
level baseline for oral microbiome research and will demonstrate clinical utility through fine-tuning for Alzheimer's
disease prediction with external and clinical validation. This research will advance understanding of oral-systemic
relationships and will establish a non-invasive, cost-effective screening tool (~$45/test) deployable in dental
clinics for Alzheimer's disease and other systemic conditions.

title: Multi-angle Total Internal Reflection Structured Illumination Microscopy to Investigate Exo-Endocytosis Coupling in Living Cells
text:
Neurons communicate by releasing chemical signals through tiny vesicles, which must be quickly recycled to
keep the brain functioning properly. Problems with this process are linked to neurological disorders such as
Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease, but scientists lack the tools to see these rapid events in living cells. This
project will develop an advanced microscope to capture these nanoscale processes in real time, providing new
insights that could lead to better treatments for brain disorders.

title: Mapping the single cell state basis of metastasis in space and time
text:
Cancer is the second leading cause of death in the United States and 90% of deaths occur at metastatic stages.
Metastasis requires the cancer cell to accomplish many distinct tasks as it moves through the body to form new
tumors in distant organs. Our proposal seeks to identify systematically how a cancer cell's molecular toolkit
changes during metastasis with the goal of identifying new therapeutic targets to prevent metastasis and for
treating patients with metastatic disease.

title: Coordination of alternative exon and 3'UTR choices in mRNAs
text:
Alternative 3' UTR usage can be coordinated with alternative upstream exon choices to generate full length
mRNAs that differ in protein-coding capacity and how they are regulated. This proposal investigates how these
choices are coordinated in single cells and tests their function in human neurons.

title: In vivo engineering of B cells for the secretion of HIV broadly neutralizing antibodies
text:
We have developed a highly novel gene therapy approach to achieve a functional cure for HIV, based on
engineering B cells ex vivo to express HIV broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnABs). The approach is well suited
for in vivo delivery because B cells are abundant and accessible in the body, and because modifying relatively
few B cells is sufficient to generate the desired therapeutic effect. Here, we further develop in vivo delivery
vectors in order to generate multi-specific bnAb responses for long-term HIV control.

title: Chronic pain conditions and internalizing psychopathology, a genetic epidemiology investigation.
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE. Over 100 million Americans and approximately 50% of U.S. military Veterans suffer
from chronic pain. Research indicates a strong, bidirectional link between chronic pain conditions and
internalizing psychiatric disorders and individuals with both chronic pain conditions and internalizing disorders
show worse treatment prognosis, increased impairment, and greater use of opioid medication. While the
association between chronic pain and internalizing disorders is well documented, the underlying mechanisms
that drive the association remain elusive. This CDA-2 project will use electronic health record and genetic data
from the Million Veterans Program to identify the genetic factors common to the development of these
conditions and sets the stage for progression from genetic epidemiology to precision medicine. Improved
understanding of the mechanism underlying this relationship can reduce negative consequences such as
opiate use, healthcare costs and societal burden, and improve access to care for Veterans.

title: DNA damaging therapy and immune response in small cell lung cancer subtypes
text:
New therapeutic strategies to enhance immunotherapy responses are desperately needed for small cell lung
cancer (SCLC), a largely immune “cold” cancer for which outcomes have remained virtually unchanged for
thirty years. Our preliminary data indicate that DNA damaging therapies (such as PARP inhibitors) may induce
changes in the immune microenvironment that are distinct between SCLC subtypes or other biomarker-defined
groups. This proposal will investigate therapeutic vulnerabilities of distinct SCLC subtypes to combinations of
DNA damaging agents or replication stress targeting with immune checkpoint blockade and has the potential to
be rapidly translated into effective, biomarker-driven approaches for patients.

title: Harnessing the Power of Data and Artificial Intelligence to Resolve the Human 3D Interactome
text:
Protein-protein interactions are essential for biological functions, and their disruption can
lead to disease. Tens of thousands of human proteins form hundreds of thousands of
interactions, and a significant fraction of these interactions remain uncharacterized. The
computational methods developed in this project will tackle critical challenges in detecting
and modeling protein-protein interactions, advance our understanding of the human
interactome, and illuminate the molecular mechanisms underlying human diseases.

title: Chromatin regulation through RNA demethylation in environmental stress response
text:
We have previously established in vitro and animal models to investigate gene expression changes induced by
arsenic and UVB stresses. The proposed research will investigate how environmental toxicants may dysregulate
chromatin-associated RNA m6A methylation to modulate cell chromatin state, leading to altered gene expression
and contributing to tumorigenesis.

title: Uncovering the role of SAP97 in synaptic function and schizophrenia.
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because dysfunction of glutamatergic neurotransmission is
believed to underlie a number of complex brain disorders including Autism Spectrum Disorder, Schizophrenia
and Alzheimer’s Disease. The proposed research is relevant to the mission of the NINDS given that knowledge
concerning how glutamatergic synapse function is regulated will aid in the development of new therapeutic
strategies for treating such disorders.

title: Immunosuppression mediated by regulatory CD8+ T cells in lung cancers
text:
While immunotherapy using immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has advanced the treatment of lung cancers, a
significant fraction of patients exhibits limited responses. We hypothesize that resistance to this therapy might
stem from regulatory CD8+ T cells, a previously underappreciated immunosuppressive cell type recently
identified as critical for peripheral tolerance in both humans and mice. Utilizing a comprehensive panel of murine
orthotopic lung cancer models, we aim to elucidate the role of regulatory CD8+ T cells in modulating anti-tumor
immunity and investigate whether depleting these cells could overcome the resistance to ICB in lung cancers.

title: Mutational scanning of seizure-related gene para in fruit flies
text:
The clinical relevance of most missense variants observed in human genes is currently unknown, because so
many possible variants exist and most have not been observed in the clinic enough times for their effect to be
known. The proposed work will enable the rapid phenotyping of thousands of gene variants in parallel in a
multicellular eukaryotic organism for the first time and will provide evidence for clinical classification of over 1,000
variants of the D. melanogaster ortholog of the very closely conserved human SCN1A gene. This technology will
improve disease screening, diagnosis, and prognosis by rapidly characterizing and annotating which variants
seen in the human genome contribute to pathogenicity.

title: CRISPR screens of population relevant genes governing toxicant resilience
text:
Genetic differences between people and populations can impact the risk of adverse effects from environmental
exposures. Improved understanding of the relationship between genetic susceptibility and the environment is
critical to protecting public health. Current approaches have had limited success in identifying human health
relevant interactions. We propose a fundamentally different approach to functional assess commonly variant
human genes for their role in specific environmental exposures which could enable more effective human risk
assessment.

title: Therapeutic targeting of SIRT3 for aggressive and refractory lymphomas
text:
SIRT3 Narrative
We discovered that the mitochondrial sirtuin SIRT3 is required to maintain the growth and
survival of DLBCLs and is especially highly expressed in those lymphomas with the worst
clinical outcome. Herein, we will develop the basis for translating SIRT3 targeted therapy to the
clinic for these chemotherapy resistant patients who have few viable therapeutic options. We
will develop SIRT3 lead compounds for clinical translation and define potential resistance
mechanism and the means to overcome them.

title: CD4 T cells and immune cell triads in anti-tumor immunity
text:
This project will determine how tumor-reactive CD4 T cells and CD8 T cells contribute to anti-tumor
immunity. This work will provide mechanistic and translational insights into the spatiotemporal and
molecular factors critical for tumor control and inform strategies to enhance immunotherapy responses.
